This site collects the reproducible analyses behind the IHC method study —
spatial single-cell IHC, bulk RNA-seq, cell-type deconvolution, clinical data,
and the image-registration / segmentation benchmarks that validate the pipeline.

The single-cell inputs come from the sibling repos: cells are segmented and
quantified by **mirage** (`../mirage`) and gated in QuPath by **FlowPath**
(`../qupath-extension-flowpath`); the benchmark tables come from mirage's
`benchmarks/` sweep. `code/cell_tables.R` reconciles the three export schemas those
tools produce, so every analysis here reads one vocabulary — see `code/README.md`.

Each analysis below is a standalone page. Start with the **Overview**, then dive
into whichever thread you need. Pages marked _(in progress)_ are authored but not
yet knit to HTML, so their links may not resolve until the next site build.

## Start here

- [Overview](overview.html) — project scope, the datasets in play, and how the
  pieces fit together.

## Method validation & QC

The core "method" contribution: how cells are assigned to tumour annotations,
how IHC markers are quality-controlled, and how the imaging pipeline is benchmarked.

- [Annotation membership QC](annotation_membership_qc.html) _(in progress)_ —
  sf point-in-polygon membership vs. the `Out_of_annotation` flag, compared per cell.
- [IHC marker QC](ihc_qc.html) _(in progress)_ — per-marker distribution and
  bimodality checks on `ihc_data`, with no external reference.
- [Registration accuracy](registration_accuracy.html) — landmark-free accuracy of
  the image registration: VALIS feature rTRE per stage, an independent
  segmentation-overlap (Dice / µm displacement) cross-check, accuracy vs cost, and
  an explicit agreement view of the two estimates. **All** registration-accuracy
  figures live here.
- [Pipeline benchmarks](benchmarks.html) — Mirage image-processing benchmark:
  resource scaling, I/O volume, whole-pipeline cost and segmentation-method
  comparison from the SLURM sweep.

## Molecular & clinical analyses

**Three clinical_data pages, one analysis.** They differ only in how a cell is
assigned to a tumour annotation. The rule is chosen in each page's setup
(`membership_data(mode, ...)` in `code/membership.R`); everything downstream is the
same document, `analysis/_clinical_data_body.Rmd`, so any difference between the
three pages is attributable to the membership rule alone.

- [Clinical data](clinical_data.html) — **geojson** membership: a cell is inside
  when its centroid falls in the pathologist polygon (sf point-in-polygon). The
  reference of the three, and the only one that knows an annotation's area, so the
  only one with cell densities.
- [Clinical data — per-annotation flag](clinical_data_per_annotation.html) —
  **flag** membership: the exporter's precomputed `Out_of_annotation`, from the
  per-annotation exports, falling back to the whole-slide csv for patients with no
  per-annotation file. Ignores `per_annotation/old/`.
- [Clinical data — per-annotation flag, `old/` overlay](clinical_data_per_annotation_old.html)
  — the same, except `per_annotation/old/` overrides the top-level file for the
  annotations it re-exports, so the diff against the page above isolates the effect
  of those re-exports.
- [Bulk RNA-seq](bulkRna.html) — DESeq2-based differential expression over the
  bulk RNA inputs.
- [Deconvolution](deconvolution.html) — cell-type deconvolution (immunedeconv),
  bridging bulk RNA (CRF-id) and IHC (patient) id spaces via the clinical table.
- [Marker exclusivity](exclusivity.html) _(in progress)_ — per-patient marker
  co-expression / lineage leakage from the whole-slide `ihc_data`.
- [Tumour border / invasive margin](periphery.html) _(in progress)_ —
  immune composition in the invasive-margin buffer around tumour annotations.
